```{r}
# Setup
library(dplyr)
library(sdmTMB)
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)

source(here::here("R", "00-settings.R"))
source(here::here("R", "functions.R"))

# @TODO - have a separate covariate extraction and joining step like I do in cod, for now keep this demo as is

```

### 1. Data preparation

* Covariates are attached with `attach_covariate()` (see `R/functions.R` for the covariate standard). Swap a source by changing its path below; nothing else in this document depends on which source it is.

* Survey points and the prediction grid come from separate inputs: the official survey grid (`demo-00-get-survey-grid.R`) carries no covariates.

* Survey sets are from `surveyjoin` (`download-surveyjoin-data.R`): one row per set with its tow date, zeros included. Columns are mapped to the names used downstream below; this is the step to adapt for your own survey data.

* Combine bottom temperature with the dogfish survey records. Sets get the layer for their own tow date.

* Combine bottom temperature with the survey grid (`demo-00-get-survey-grid.R`). The grid has no dates, so it is assigned the `predict_month` and the covariate values are extracted based on this.

* Visual check: map dogfish observations and temperature patterns by year for the full survey and for one region (WCVI)

```{r}
species <- "dogfish"
# species <- "pacific-cod" # requires stored dataset

# Inputs: change these to swap the survey data, grid or a covariate source
sets_file <- file.path(data_gen_dir, "dogfish-syn-wcvi-sets.rds") # committed; from download-surveyjoin-data.R
# sets_file <- file.path(data_gen_dir, "dogfish-survey-sets.rds") # all surveys: run download-surveyjoin-data.R
grid_file <- file.path(data_gen_dir, "dogfish-poly-grid.rds") # sf polygons, geometry only; from demo-00-get-survey-grid.R

# Choose depth source (GEBCO is probably going to be standard)
depth_file <- file.path(data_raw_dir, "gebco-depth.nc") # static; see demo-00-get-GEBCO.R
# depth_file <- file.path(data_gen_dir, "trond-depth.nc") # see format-trond.R

# Choose bottom temperature source
temp_file <- file.path(data_raw_dir, "glorys-bottom-temp-monthly.nc") # monthly; see demo-00-get-GLORYS.R
# temp_file <- file.path(data_gen_dir, "trond-bottom-temp-june-yearly.nc") # one layer per year; see format-trond.R

# Prediction month for monthly covariates. Sets get the layer for their own tow
# date; the grid has no dates, so it gets this month's layer in each year.
# - No season term in the model (dogfish example): the month the survey mostly
#   samples, so covariate effects are predicted at the conditions they were
#   estimated under.
# - Season factor in the model: pick the reference season, add it to the grid
#   (prediction-grid chunk), and set this to the month within that season that
#   its sets mostly fall in, so temperature and season refer to the same time
#   (e.g. 7 with season = "Summer" for the July DFO Maritimes survey).
# - Only yearly covariates: NULL.
# - One month only. `attach_covariate()` can average several months, but the
#   bottom-temperature map below assumes one layer per year.
predict_month <- 6 # SYN WCVI sets are late May to June

# Surveys to model. The dogfish grid falls entirely within the WCVI synoptic
# survey; modelling more surveys also needs a grid that covers them.
surveys_use <- "SYN WCVI"
# surveys_use <- c("SYN WCVI", "SYN QCS", "SYN HS", "SYN WCHG") # all BC synoptic; needs the all-surveys file
# Not carried by the official grid: the survey level to predict at
grid_survey_abbrev <- "SYN WCVI"

# Covariate years: survey years through a forecast horizon (the covariate may go to 2099)
forecast_end_year <- 2060

# Attached to every saved object and checked downstream (check_data_sources()):
# outputs use fixed filenames, so a re-render with other sources overwrites them
data_sources <- list(
  sets = basename(sets_file),
  surveys = surveys_use,
  grid = basename(grid_file),
  grid_survey = grid_survey_abbrev,
  depth = basename(depth_file),
  bottom_temp = basename(temp_file),
  predict_month = predict_month,
  forecast_end_year = forecast_end_year,
  created = Sys.time()
)

sets <- readRDS(sets_file) |>
  filter(survey_name %in% surveys_use)
if (any(sets$effort_units != "ha")) {
  cli::cli_abort("Expected effort in ha; got {.val {unique(sets$effort_units)}}.")
}

# Map the survey's columns to the names used downstream: catch_weight (kg),
# area_swept (km2, for the offset), and X/Y (km) in the grid's CRS so sets and
# grid share coordinates. Sets keep their tow date, which picks the matching
# month of a monthly covariate.
# Depth for the fit comes from depth_file, extracted the same way as on the
# grid, so the model is fit and predicted with one depth source. The recorded
# set depth is kept as depth_recorded for comparison only.
dat_sf <- sets |>
  transmute(
    survey_abbrev = factor(survey_name),
    event_id,
    year,
    date = as.Date(date),
    longitude = lon_start,
    latitude = lat_start,
    depth_recorded = depth_m,
    catch_weight,
    area_swept = effort / 100 # ha to km2
  ) |>
  sdmTMB::add_utm_columns(
    ll_names = c("longitude", "latitude"),
    utm_crs = utm_crs,
    units = "km"
  ) |>
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE) |>
  attach_covariate(depth_file, "depth_m", method = "bilinear") |>
  attach_covariate(temp_file, "bottom_temp", date_col = "date") |>
  filter(depth_m > 0) |> # also drops sets outside the depth raster (NA)
  filter(!is.na(bottom_temp)) |> # e.g. inshore sets outside the temperature model's ocean cells
  mutate(log_depth = log(depth_m))

dat <- sf::st_drop_geometry(dat_sf)

glimpse(dat)
```

```{r}
#| label: wcvi-survey-set-bottom-temp

ggplot(dat_sf) +
  geom_sf(data = pacea::bc_coast) +
  geom_sf(aes(colour = bottom_temp)) +
  viridis::scale_colour_viridis(option = "plasma") +
  facet_wrap(~ year) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 3)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 2)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  ggtitle("Survey set bottom temperatures") +
  viridis::scale_colour_viridis(
    option = "plasma",
    name = "Bottom temperature (°C)",
    guide = guide_colourbar(
      barwidth = unit(6, "cm"),
      barheight = unit(0.4, "cm"),
      title.vjust = 0.9,
      direction = "horizontal"
    )
  ) +
  gfplot::coord_sf_auto(dat_sf, buffer = 10000)
```

### Prediction grid

* The grid file (`demo-00-get-survey-grid.R`) is already split by region: one row per `cell` x `region`, with `cell`, `X`/`Y` (km) and `area` (km²) assigned there. Cells straddling a region boundary have one row per region, each with its own `area`, sharing the parent `cell` id and one `X`/`Y` (the centroid of the whole cell).

* Each cell gets depth and bottom temperature (all years) from the covariate files, extracted once per cell at that shared `X`/`Y` and joined back to the region pieces by `cell`. Both halves of a split cell therefore get the same covariate values.

```{r}
grid <- readRDS(grid_file)
# Set X/Y (utm_crs, 00-settings.R) and grid X/Y must share a CRS for the mesh
# and predictions to line up
if (sf::st_crs(grid) != sf::st_crs(utm_crs)) {
  cli::cli_abort("{.file {basename(grid_file)}} is not in {.code utm_crs} (EPSG:{utm_crs}); rebuild it with {.file demo-00-get-survey-grid.R}.")
}

# Centroids of the whole (unsplit) cells; the covariates are attached here and
# joined back to the region pieces by `cell`.
grid_covariates <- grid |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  distinct(cell, X, Y) |>
  mutate(x_m = X * 1000, y_m = Y * 1000) |> # grid CRS is in m
  sf::st_as_sf(coords = c("x_m", "y_m"), crs = sf::st_crs(grid)) |>
  attach_covariate(depth_file, "depth_m", method = "bilinear") |>
  attach_covariate(temp_file, "bottom_temp", method = "simple", month = predict_month) |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  filter(year >= min(dat$year), year <= forecast_end_year) |>
  mutate(log_depth = ifelse(depth_m > 0, log(depth_m), NA_real_)) # cells above sea level have no log depth

grid_covariates |>
  filter(year == min(year)) |>
  summarise(n_cells = n(), na_depth = sum(is.na(log_depth)), na_temp = sum(is.na(bottom_temp)))
```

```{r}
#| label: bottom-temp-map

# crop for faster plotting of the grid extent only
temp_rast <- terra::rast(temp_file)
temp_time <- terra::time(temp_rast)
temp_keep <- as.integer(format(temp_time, "%Y")) %in% seq(min(dat$year), forecast_end_year, by = 4)
if (!is.null(predict_month)) temp_keep <- temp_keep & as.integer(format(temp_time, "%m")) %in% predict_month
temp_plot <- temp_rast[[temp_keep]] |>
  terra::crop(terra::vect(sf::st_transform(grid, terra::crs(temp_rast))))
names(temp_plot) <- format(terra::time(temp_plot), "%Y")

ggplot() +
  tidyterra::geom_spatraster(data = temp_plot) +
  geom_sf(data = pacea::bc_coast) +
  facet_wrap(~lyr) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 3)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(n = 2)) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
  ggtitle(paste("Bottom temperature on the grid:", if (is.null(predict_month)) "yearly layers" else month.name[predict_month])) +
  viridis::scale_fill_viridis(
    option = "plasma",
    name = "Bottom temperature (°C)",
    na.value = "transparent",
    guide = guide_colourbar(
      barwidth = unit(6, "cm"),
      barheight = unit(0.4, "cm"),
      title.vjust = 0.9,
      direction = "horizontal"
    )
  ) +
  coord_sf(
    xlim = sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(grid, 4326))[c("xmin", "xmax")],
    ylim = sf::st_bbox(sf::st_transform(grid, 4326))[c("ymin", "ymax")]
  )
```

### Assemble the prediction grid

* Regions come with the grid (`demo-00-get-survey-grid.R`): here a toy N/S split of WCVI (`R/make-wcvi-region-polygons.R`) to work through multi-region indicators downstream. A split cell contributes one row per region, each with its own `area` and the shared per-cell covariates.

```{r}
#| label: prediction-grid

cell_polygons <- grid |>
  # one survey level for the whole grid; same levels as the sets so a
  # multi-survey model can predict at it
  mutate(survey_abbrev = factor(grid_survey_abbrev, levels = levels(dat$survey_abbrev))) |>
  relocate(survey_abbrev, .after = region)
  # With a season factor in the model, add the season that predict_month falls in, e.g.
  # mutate(season = factor("summer", levels = levels(dat$season)))

# Make prediction grid data.frame (keep this object lean because it is expanded to all years)
prediction_grid <- cell_polygons |>
  sf::st_drop_geometry() |>
  left_join(grid_covariates, by = c("cell", "X", "Y"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  select(cell, region, survey_abbrev, area, X, Y, depth_m, log_depth, year, bottom_temp) |>
  filter(!is.na(bottom_temp), !is.na(log_depth), !is.infinite(log_depth))

# Check prediction grid
cell_polygons |>
  select(cell, region, geometry) |>
  left_join(
    prediction_grid |> filter(year == max(dat$year) + 1),
    by = c("cell", "region")
  ) |>
  ggplot() +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = depth_m, colour = region))

unique(prediction_grid$year)

```

### Save prepared data for species distribution modelling

```{r}
attr(dat, "data_sources") <- data_sources
attr(cell_polygons, "data_sources") <- data_sources
attr(prediction_grid, "data_sources") <- data_sources

out_filename <- paste0(species, ".rds")
# Objects saved
# - cleaned survey data
saveRDS(dat, file = file.path(model_input_dir, out_filename))

# - minimize object sizes: rasterized cell polygons (keyed by `cell`/`region`)
# - join downstream for plotting / sf uses
# @TODO: might make sense to make this a standard filename
saveRDS(cell_polygons, file = file.path(model_input_dir, "wcvi-cell-polygons.rds"))

# - prediction grid data.frame
saveRDS(prediction_grid, file = file.path(model_input_dir, "prediction-grid.rds"))
```

* Species survey data with covariate data (bottom temperature and depth) [data.frame]

* Prediction grid (depth + bottom temperature, all forecast years) [data.frame], keyed by `cell`/`region`

* Cell polygons keyed by `cell`/`region` [sf], for joining predictions back to polygons for plotting

* Each carries a `data_sources` attribute (survey, grid and covariate files); `check_data_sources()` in 02 and 03 confirms they match
